title: Derived base change of a polynomial differential complex
statement:
Let $A\to C$, $A\to A'$, $f:C\to C'$ and $A'\to C'$ be a commutative square of commutative rings, and let $P_\bullet\to C$ be an augmented simplicial $A$-algebra whose terms are polynomial algebras $P_n=A[x_i\mid i\in I_n]$, for arbitrary sets $I_n$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. No resolution condition is imposed. Give $P'_\bullet=P_\bullet\otimes_A A'$ the augmentation $p\otimes a'\mapsto f(\epsilon(p))a'$. Use the alternating-complex convention $s(M)^{-n}=M_n$, differential $\sum_i(-1)^id_i$ and zero positive terms [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence], and Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Put $K=s(\Omega^1_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}C)$ and $K'=s(\Omega^1_{P'_\bullet/A'}\otimes_{P'_\bullet}C')$. Every term of $K$ is a flat $C$-module and $K$ is K-flat [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. There is a canonical isomorphism in $D(C')$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]
$$\Theta:QK\otimes_C^{\mathbf L}C'\xrightarrow{\sim}QK'.$$
Here derived scalar extension is interpreted through [lem-trf-one-point-derived-ring-identification]. More precisely, if $c_K:QK\otimes_C^{\mathbf L}C'\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(K\otimes_C C')$ is its canonical K-flat computation isomorphism, then $\Theta=Q(\theta)c_K$, where $\theta:K\otimes_C C'\xrightarrow{\sim}K'$ is a chain isomorphism represented on differential generators by
$$(\mathrm dp\otimes c)\otimes b'\longmapsto\mathrm d(p\otimes1)\otimes f(c)b'.$$
Its component maps commute with every face and degeneracy of the differential modules. Tensor products mean [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. This holds for empty and infinite variable sets and without flatness of either ring map. Flat modules are as in [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and simplicial objects and their morphisms are as in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object].

source.place: Tag 08QQ (lemma-flat-base-change-cotangent-complex), proof: flatness of the polynomial differential module and its identification after scalar extension, written in the alternating polynomial-resolution model.

proof.text: For every $n$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables] to $P_n=A[x_i\mid i\in I_n]$ and its augmentation to $C$. After interchanging the tensor factors, $K^{-n}=\Omega^1_{P_n/A}\otimes_{P_n}C$ has $C$-basis $e_i=\mathrm dx_i\otimes1$. This module is flat directly from [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]: for an injection $N\to N'$, identify $N\otimes_C K^{-n}$ with the finitely supported families $\bigoplus_{i\in I_n}N$ by $z\otimes\sum c_i e_i\mapsto(c_i z)_i$, with inverse $(z_i)_i\mapsto\sum z_i\otimes e_i$, using [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The induced map is coordinatewise the given injection, hence injective. The zero positive terms are flat by the same argument with the empty basis.

source.place: Tag 00RX, lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring, proof; arbitrary-variable basis as in the cited node; definition-flat (00HB).

proof.text: The alternating-complex convention puts $K$ in degrees at most zero. The identification $N\otimes_CK^{-n}\cong\bigoplus_{i\in I_n}N$ of step 1 is natural in $N$, so tensoring with $K^{-n}$ carries a sequence $N_1\to N_2\to N_3$ exact at $N_2$ to its coordinatewise direct sum, which is exact; thus each term is flat also in the exact-sequence sense of [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat]. Together with step 1 this satisfies exactly the hypotheses of [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat], with $R=C$ and upper bound $0$. Its conclusion makes $K$ K-flat in the ordinary-module sense.

Regard $P_\bullet$ as augmented to $C'$ by $f\epsilon$. Put $L=s(\Omega^1_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}C')$. The tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives mutually inverse maps $a_n:(\Omega^1_{P_n/A}\otimes_{P_n}C)\otimes_C C'\to\Omega^1_{P_n/A}\otimes_{P_n}C'$ and $b_n$ by $a_n((\omega\otimes c)\otimes b')=\omega\otimes f(c)b'$ and $b_n(\omega\otimes b')=(\omega\otimes1)\otimes b'$. Balancing over $P_n$ uses its augmentation to $C$, and balancing over $C$ uses $f$; these relations also show $b_na_n=a_nb_n=1$. For any face or degeneracy $u:P_n\to P_m$, both orders send $(\mathrm dp\otimes c)\otimes b'$ to $\mathrm d(u(p))\otimes f(c)b'$. Such generators span by [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Thus $a$ commutes with all these operators and their signed sums, giving a chain isomorphism $a:K\otimes_C C'\to L$.

source.place: Tag 08QQ, lemma-flat-base-change-cotangent-complex, coefficient identification in the proof; explicit tensor-balancing verification.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-simplicial-differential-base-change] with $R=A$, $R'=A'$, $T=C'$ and augmentation $f\epsilon$. The ring square makes $f\epsilon$ an augmentation compatible with $A\to A'\to C'$; its scalar extension is exactly $p\otimes a'\mapsto f(\epsilon(p))a'$. The cited lemma gives a chain isomorphism $v:L\to K'$ commuting with all faces and degeneracies, with $v(\mathrm dp\otimes t)=\mathrm d(p\otimes1)\otimes t$. Set $\theta=va$. Its formula is therefore $(\mathrm dp\otimes c)\otimes b'\mapsto\mathrm d(p\otimes1)\otimes f(c)b'$, and both component isomorphisms commute with every simplicial operator. The cited lemma requires neither flatness nor a resolution.

source.place: Tag 00RV, lemma-differentials-base-change, universal-derivation formula, applied simplicially as in the cited node.

proof.text: Use the identity resolution $K\xrightarrow{1}K$, which is K-flat by step 2. Clause (2) of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], transported to ordinary modules by [lem-trf-one-point-derived-ring-identification], gives the canonical computation isomorphism $c_K:QK\otimes_C^{\mathbf L}C'\to Q(K\otimes_C C')$. Localization $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] sends the inverse chain maps $\theta,\theta^{-1}$ to inverse maps, so $\Theta=Q(\theta)c_K$ is an isomorphism in $D(C')$. This is the specified canonical comparison. All arguments use finite-support tensor expressions, even when $I_n$ is infinite; for empty $I_n$ the differential module is zero. No step assumes that $P_\bullet\to C$ resolves $C$, that the augmentation is surjective, or that either ring map is flat.
